1.web: God, having in the past spoken to the fathers through the prophets at many times and in various ways,
1.kjv: God, who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets,
1.bsb: On many past occasions and in many different ways, God spoke to our fathers through the prophets.

1.web: has at the end of these days spoken to us by his Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, through whom also he made the worlds.
1.kjv: Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds;
1.bsb: But in these last days He has spoken to us by His Son, whom He appointed heir of all things, and through whom He made the universe.

1.web: His Son is the radiance of his glory, the very image of his substance, and upholding all things by the word of his power, who, when he had by himself purified us of our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;
1.kjv: Who being the brightness of his glory, and the express image of his person, and upholding all things by the word of his power, when he had by himself purged our sins, sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high;
1.bsb: The Son is the radiance of God’s glory and the exact representation of His nature, upholding all things by His powerful word. After He had provided purification for sins, He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.

1.web: having become so much better than the angels, as he has inherited a more excellent name than they have.
1.kjv: Being made so much better than the angels, as he hath by inheritance obtained a more excellent name than they.
1.bsb: So He became as far superior to the angels as the name He has inherited is excellent beyond theirs.

1.web: For to which of the angels did he say at any time, “You are my Son. Today I have become your father?” and again, “I will be to him a Father, and he will be to me a Son?”
1.kjv: For unto which of the angels said he at any time, Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee? And again, I will be to him a Father, and he shall be to me a Son?
1.bsb: For to which of the angels did God ever say: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father”? Or again: “I will be His Father, and He will be My Son”?

1.web: When he again brings in the firstborn into the world he says, “Let all the angels of God worship him.”
1.kjv: And again, when he bringeth in the firstbegotten into the world, he saith, And let all the angels of God worship him.
1.bsb: And again, when God brings His firstborn into the world, He says: “Let all God’s angels worship Him.”

1.web: Of the angels he says, “Who makes his angels winds, and his servants a flame of fire.”
1.kjv: And of the angels he saith, Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire.
1.bsb: Now about the angels He says: “He makes His angels winds, His servants flames of fire.”

1.web: But of the Son he says, “Your throne, O God, is forever and ever. The scepter of uprightness is the scepter of your Kingdom.
1.kjv: But unto the Son he saith , Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: a sceptre of righteousness is the sceptre of thy kingdom.
1.bsb: But about the Son He says: “Your throne, O God, endures forever and ever, and justice is the scepter of Your kingdom.

1.web: You have loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows.”
1.kjv: Thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity; therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows.
1.bsb: You have loved righteousness and hated wickedness; therefore God, Your God, has anointed You above Your companions with the oil of joy.”

1.web: And, “You, Lord, in the beginning, laid the foundation of the earth. The heavens are the works of your hands.
1.kjv: And, Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth; and the heavens are the works of thine hands:
1.bsb: And: “In the beginning, O Lord, You laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of Your hands.

1.web: They will perish, but you continue. They all will grow old like a garment does.
1.kjv: They shall perish; but thou remainest; and they all shall wax old as doth a garment;
1.bsb: They will perish, but You remain; they will all wear out like a garment.

1.web: You will roll them up like a mantle, and they will be changed; but you are the same. Your years will not fail.”
1.kjv: And as a vesture shalt thou fold them up, and they shall be changed: but thou art the same, and thy years shall not fail.
1.bsb: You will roll them up like a robe; like a garment they will be changed; but You remain the same, and Your years will never end.”

1.web: But which of the angels has he told at any time, “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies the footstool of your feet?”
1.kjv: But to which of the angels said he at any time, Sit on my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool?
1.bsb: Yet to which of the angels did God ever say: “Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet”?

1.web: Aren’t they all serving spirits, sent out to do service for the sake of those who will inherit salvation?
1.kjv: Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?
1.bsb: Are not the angels ministering spirits sent to serve those who will inherit salvation?

2.web: Therefore we ought to pay greater attention to the things that were heard, lest perhaps we drift away.
2.kjv: Therefore we ought to give the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard, lest at any time we should let them slip.
2.bsb: We must pay closer attention, therefore, to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away.

2.web: For if the word spoken through angels proved steadfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompense;
2.kjv: For if the word spoken by angels was stedfast, and every transgression and disobedience received a just recompence of reward;
2.bsb: For if the message spoken by angels was binding, and every transgression and disobedience received its just punishment,

2.web: how will we escape if we neglect so great a salvation—which at the first having been spoken through the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard;
2.kjv: How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation; which at the first began to be spoken by the Lord, and was confirmed unto us by them that heard him ;
2.bsb: how shall we escape if we neglect such a great salvation? This salvation was first announced by the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard Him,

2.web: God also testifying with them, both by signs and wonders, by various works of power, and by gifts of the Holy Spirit, according to his own will?
2.kjv: God also bearing them witness, both with signs and wonders, and with divers miracles, and gifts of the Holy Ghost, according to his own will?
2.bsb: and was affirmed by God through signs, wonders, various miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to His will.

2.web: For he didn’t subject the world to come, of which we speak, to angels.
2.kjv: For unto the angels hath he not put in subjection the world to come, whereof we speak.
2.bsb: For it is not to angels that He has subjected the world to come, about which we are speaking.

2.web: But one has somewhere testified, saying, “What is man, that you think of him? Or the son of man, that you care for him?
2.kjv: But one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man, that thou visitest him?
2.bsb: But somewhere it is testified in these words: “What is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?

2.web: You made him a little lower than the angels. You crowned him with glory and honor.
2.kjv: Thou madest him a little lower than the angels; thou crownedst him with glory and honour, and didst set him over the works of thy hands:
2.bsb: You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor

2.web: You have put all things in subjection under his feet.” For in that he subjected all things to him, he left nothing that is not subject to him. But now we don’t see all things subjected to him, yet.
2.kjv: Thou hast put all things in subjection under his feet. For in that he put all in subjection under him, he left nothing that is not put under him. But now we see not yet all things put under him.
2.bsb: and placed everything under his feet.” When God subjected all things to him, He left nothing outside of his control. Yet at present we do not see everything subject to him.

2.web: But we see him who has been made a little lower than the angels, Jesus, because of the suffering of death crowned with glory and honor, that by the grace of God he should taste of death for everyone.
2.kjv: But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.
2.bsb: But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because He suffered death, so that by the grace of God He might taste death for everyone.

2.web: For it became him, for whom are all things, and through whom are all things, in bringing many children to glory, to make the author of their salvation perfect through sufferings.
2.kjv: For it became him, for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, in bringing many sons unto glory, to make the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.
2.bsb: In bringing many sons to glory, it was fitting for God, for whom and through whom all things exist, to make the author of their salvation perfect through suffering.

2.web: For both he who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all from one, for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brothers,
2.kjv: For both he that sanctifieth and they who are sanctified are all of one: for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren,
2.bsb: For both the One who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are of the same family. So Jesus is not ashamed to call them brothers.

2.web: saying, “I will declare your name to my brothers. Among of the congregation I will sing your praise.”
2.kjv: Saying, I will declare thy name unto my brethren, in the midst of the church will I sing praise unto thee.
2.bsb: He says: “I will proclaim Your name to My brothers; I will sing Your praises in the assembly.”

2.web: Again, “I will put my trust in him.” Again, “Behold, here I am with the children whom God has given me.”
2.kjv: And again, I will put my trust in him. And again, Behold I and the children which God hath given me.
2.bsb: And again: “I will put My trust in Him.” And once again: “Here am I, and the children God has given Me.”

2.web: Since then the children have shared in flesh and blood, he also himself in the same way partook of the same, that through death he might bring to nothing him who had the power of death, that is, the devil,
2.kjv: Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;
2.bsb: Now since the children have flesh and blood, He too shared in their humanity, so that by His death He might destroy him who holds the power of death, that is, the devil,

2.web: and might deliver all of them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.
2.kjv: And deliver them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage.
2.bsb: and free those who all their lives were held in slavery by their fear of death.

2.web: For most certainly, he doesn’t give help to angels, but he gives help to the offspring of Abraham.
2.kjv: For verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham.
2.bsb: For surely it is not the angels He helps, but the descendants of Abraham.

2.web: Therefore he was obligated in all things to be made like his brothers, that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make atonement for the sins of the people.
2.kjv: Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.
2.bsb: For this reason He had to be made like His brothers in every way, so that He might become a merciful and faithful high priest in service to God, in order to make atonement for the sins of the people.

2.web: For in that he himself has suffered being tempted, he is able to help those who are tempted.
2.kjv: For in that he himself hath suffered being tempted, he is able to succour them that are tempted.
2.bsb: Because He Himself suffered when He was tempted, He is able to help those who are being tempted.

3.web: Therefore, holy brothers, partakers of a heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our confession, Jesus;
3.kjv: Wherefore, holy brethren, partakers of the heavenly calling, consider the Apostle and High Priest of our profession, Christ Jesus;
3.bsb: Therefore, holy brothers, who share in the heavenly calling, set your focus on Jesus, the apostle and high priest whom we confess.

3.web: who was faithful to him who appointed him, as also was Moses in all his house.
3.kjv: Who was faithful to him that appointed him, as also Moses was faithful in all his house.
3.bsb: He was faithful to the One who appointed Him, just as Moses was faithful in all God’s house.

3.web: For he has been counted worthy of more glory than Moses, because he who built the house has more honor than the house.
3.kjv: For this man was counted worthy of more glory than Moses, inasmuch as he who hath builded the house hath more honour than the house.
3.bsb: For Jesus has been counted worthy of greater glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house has greater honor than the house itself.

3.web: For every house is built by someone; but he who built all things is God.
3.kjv: For every house is builded by some man ; but he that built all things is God.
3.bsb: And every house is built by someone, but God is the builder of everything.

3.web: Moses indeed was faithful in all his house as a servant, for a testimony of those things which were afterward to be spoken,
3.kjv: And Moses verily was faithful in all his house, as a servant, for a testimony of those things which were to be spoken after;
3.bsb: Now Moses was faithful as a servant in all God’s house, testifying to what would be spoken later.

3.web: but Christ is faithful as a Son over his house; whose house we are, if we hold fast our confidence and the glorying of our hope firm to the end.
3.kjv: But Christ as a son over his own house; whose house are we, if we hold fast the confidence and the rejoicing of the hope firm unto the end.
3.bsb: But Christ is faithful as the Son over God’s house. And we are His house, if we hold firmly to our confidence and the hope of which we boast.

3.web: Therefore, even as the Holy Spirit says, “Today if you will hear his voice,
3.kjv: Wherefore (as the Holy Ghost saith, To day if ye will hear his voice,
3.bsb: Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says: “Today, if you hear His voice,

3.web: don’t harden your hearts, as in the rebellion, like as in the day of the trial in the wilderness,
3.kjv: Harden not your hearts, as in the provocation, in the day of temptation in the wilderness:
3.bsb: do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion, in the day of testing in the wilderness,

3.web: where your fathers tested me by proving me, and saw my deeds for forty years.
3.kjv: When your fathers tempted me, proved me, and saw my works forty years.
3.bsb: where your fathers tested and tried Me, and for forty years saw My works.

3.web: Therefore I was displeased with that generation, and said, ‘They always err in their heart, but they didn’t know my ways;’
3.kjv: Wherefore I was grieved with that generation, and said, They do alway err in their heart; and they have not known my ways.
3.bsb: Therefore I was angry with that generation, and I said, ‘Their hearts are always going astray, and they have not known My ways.’

3.web: as I swore in my wrath, ‘They will not enter into my rest.’”
3.kjv: So I sware in my wrath, They shall not enter into my rest.)
3.bsb: So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’”

3.web: Beware, brothers, lest perhaps there be in any one of you an evil heart of unbelief, in falling away from the living God;
3.kjv: Take heed, brethren, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief, in departing from the living God.
3.bsb: See to it, brothers, that none of you has a wicked heart of unbelief that turns away from the living God.

3.web: but exhort one another day by day, so long as it is called “today”; lest any one of you be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
3.kjv: But exhort one another daily, while it is called To day; lest any of you be hardened through the deceitfulness of sin.
3.bsb: But exhort one another daily, as long as it is called today, so that none of you may be hardened by sin’s deceitfulness.

3.web: For we have become partakers of Christ, if we hold fast the beginning of our confidence firm to the end:
3.kjv: For we are made partakers of Christ, if we hold the beginning of our confidence stedfast unto the end;
3.bsb: We have come to share in Christ if we hold firmly to the end the assurance we had at first.

3.web: while it is said, “Today if you will hear his voice, don’t harden your hearts, as in the rebellion.”
3.kjv: While it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts, as in the provocation.
3.bsb: As it has been said: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts, as you did in the rebellion.”

3.web: For who, when they heard, rebelled? No, didn’t all those who came out of Egypt by Moses?
3.kjv: For some, when they had heard, did provoke: howbeit not all that came out of Egypt by Moses.
3.bsb: For who were the ones who heard and rebelled? Were they not all those Moses led out of Egypt?

3.web: With whom was he displeased forty years? Wasn’t it with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?
3.kjv: But with whom was he grieved forty years? was it not with them that had sinned, whose carcases fell in the wilderness?
3.bsb: And with whom was God angry for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the wilderness?

3.web: To whom did he swear that they wouldn’t enter into his rest, but to those who were disobedient?
3.kjv: And to whom sware he that they should not enter into his rest, but to them that believed not?
3.bsb: And to whom did He swear that they would never enter His rest? Was it not to those who disobeyed?

3.web: We see that they were not able to enter in because of unbelief.
3.kjv: So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief.
3.bsb: So we see that it was because of their unbelief that they were unable to enter.

4.web: Let us fear therefore, lest perhaps anyone of you should seem to have come short of a promise of entering into his rest.
4.kjv: Let us therefore fear, lest, a promise being left us of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to come short of it.
4.bsb: Therefore, while the promise of entering His rest still stands, let us be careful that none of you be deemed to have fallen short of it.

4.web: For indeed we have had good news preached to us, even as they also did, but the word they heard didn’t profit them, because it wasn’t mixed with faith by those who heard.
4.kjv: For unto us was the gospel preached, as well as unto them: but the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it .
4.bsb: For we also received the good news just as they did; but the message they heard was of no value to them, since they did not share the faith of those who comprehended it.

4.web: For we who have believed do enter into that rest, even as he has said, “As I swore in my wrath, they will not enter into my rest”; although the works were finished from the foundation of the world.
4.kjv: For we which have believed do enter into rest, as he said, As I have sworn in my wrath, if they shall enter into my rest: although the works were finished from the foundation of the world.
4.bsb: Now we who have believed enter that rest. As for the others, it is just as God has said: “So I swore on oath in My anger, ‘They shall never enter My rest.’” And yet His works have been finished since the foundation of the world.

4.web: For he has said this somewhere about the seventh day, “God rested on the seventh day from all his works”;
4.kjv: For he spake in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.
4.bsb: For somewhere He has spoken about the seventh day in this manner: “And on the seventh day God rested from all His works.”

4.web: and in this place again, “They will not enter into my rest.”
4.kjv: And in this place again, If they shall enter into my rest.
4.bsb: And again, as He says in the passage above: “They shall never enter My rest.”

4.web: Seeing therefore it remains that some should enter into it, and they to whom the good news was preached before failed to enter in because of disobedience,
4.kjv: Seeing therefore it remaineth that some must enter therein, and they to whom it was first preached entered not in because of unbelief:
4.bsb: Since, then, it remains for some to enter His rest, and since those who formerly heard the good news did not enter because of their disobedience,

4.web: he again defines a certain day, today, saying through David so long a time afterward (just as has been said), “Today if you will hear his voice, don’t harden your hearts.”
4.kjv: Again, he limiteth a certain day, saying in David, To day, after so long a time; as it is said, To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts.
4.bsb: God again designated a certain day as “Today,” when a long time later He spoke through David as was just stated: “Today, if you hear His voice, do not harden your hearts.”

4.web: For if Joshua had given them rest, he would not have spoken afterward of another day.
4.kjv: For if Jesus had given them rest, then would he not afterward have spoken of another day.
4.bsb: For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken later about another day.

4.web: There remains therefore a Sabbath rest for the people of God.
4.kjv: There remaineth therefore a rest to the people of God.
4.bsb: There remains, then, a Sabbath rest for the people of God.

4.web: For he who has entered into his rest has himself also rested from his works, as God did from his.
4.kjv: For he that is entered into his rest, he also hath ceased from his own works, as God did from his.
4.bsb: For whoever enters God’s rest also rests from his own work, just as God did from His.

4.web: Let us therefore give diligence to enter into that rest, lest anyone fall after the same example of disobedience.
4.kjv: Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.
4.bsb: Let us, therefore, make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one will fall by following the same pattern of disobedience.

4.web: For the word of God is living and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing even to the dividing of soul and spirit, of both joints and marrow, and is able to discern the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
4.kjv: For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.
4.bsb: For the word of God is living and active. Sharper than any double-edged sword, it pierces even to dividing soul and spirit, joints and marrow. It judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart.

4.web: There is no creature that is hidden from his sight, but all things are naked and laid open before the eyes of him to whom we must give an account.
4.kjv: Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.
4.bsb: Nothing in all creation is hidden from God’s sight; everything is uncovered and exposed before the eyes of Him to whom we must give account.

4.web: Having then a great high priest, who has passed through the heavens, Jesus, the Son of God, let us hold tightly to our confession.
4.kjv: Seeing then that we have a great high priest, that is passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our profession.
4.bsb: Therefore, since we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold firmly to what we profess.

4.web: For we don’t have a high priest who can’t be touched with the feeling of our infirmities, but one who has been in all points tempted like we are, yet without sin.
4.kjv: For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.
4.bsb: For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who was tempted in every way that we are, yet was without sin.

4.web: Let us therefore draw near with boldness to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy, and may find grace for help in time of need.
4.kjv: Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need.
4.bsb: Let us then approach the throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need.

5.web: For every high priest, being taken from among men, is appointed for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins.
5.kjv: For every high priest taken from among men is ordained for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins:
5.bsb: Every high priest is appointed from among men to represent them in matters relating to God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.

5.web: The high priest can deal gently with those who are ignorant and going astray, because he himself is also surrounded with weakness.
5.kjv: Who can have compassion on the ignorant, and on them that are out of the way; for that he himself also is compassed with infirmity.
5.bsb: He is able to deal gently with those who are ignorant and misguided, since he himself is beset by weakness.

5.web: Because of this, he must offer sacrifices for sins for the people, as well as for himself.
5.kjv: And by reason hereof he ought, as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins.
5.bsb: That is why he is obligated to offer sacrifices for his own sins, as well as for the sins of the people.

5.web: Nobody takes this honor on himself, but he is called by God, just like Aaron was.
5.kjv: And no man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as was Aaron.
5.bsb: No one takes this honor upon himself; he must be called by God, just as Aaron was.

5.web: So also Christ didn’t glorify himself to be made a high priest, but it was he who said to him, “You are my Son. Today I have become your father.”
5.kjv: So also Christ glorified not himself to be made an high priest; but he that said unto him, Thou art my Son, to day have I begotten thee.
5.bsb: So also Christ did not take upon Himself the glory of becoming a high priest, but He was called by the One who said to Him: “You are My Son; today I have become Your Father.”

5.web: As he says also in another place, “You are a priest forever, after the order of Melchizedek.”
5.kjv: As he saith also in another place , Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
5.bsb: And in another passage God says: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”

5.web: He, in the days of his flesh, having offered up prayers and petitions with strong crying and tears to him who was able to save him from death, and having been heard for his godly fear,
5.kjv: Who in the days of his flesh, when he had offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears unto him that was able to save him from death, and was heard in that he feared;
5.bsb: During the days of Jesus’ earthly life, He offered up prayers and petitions with loud cries and tears to the One who could save Him from death, and He was heard because of His reverence.

5.web: though he was a Son, yet learned obedience by the things which he suffered.
5.kjv: Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered;
5.bsb: Although He was a Son, He learned obedience from what He suffered.

5.web: Having been made perfect, he became to all of those who obey him the author of eternal salvation,
5.kjv: And being made perfect, he became the author of eternal salvation unto all them that obey him;
5.bsb: And having been made perfect, He became the source of eternal salvation to all who obey Him

5.web: named by God a high priest after the order of Melchizedek.
5.kjv: Called of God an high priest after the order of Melchisedec.
5.bsb: and was designated by God as high priest in the order of Melchizedek.

5.web: About him we have many words to say, and hard to interpret, seeing you have become dull of hearing.
5.kjv: Of whom we have many things to say, and hard to be uttered, seeing ye are dull of hearing.
5.bsb: We have much to say about this, but it is hard to explain, because you are dull of hearing.

5.web: For although by this time you should be teachers, you again need to have someone teach you the rudiments of the first principles of the revelations of God. You have come to need milk, and not solid food.
5.kjv: For when for the time ye ought to be teachers, ye have need that one teach you again which be the first principles of the oracles of God; and are become such as have need of milk, and not of strong meat.
5.bsb: Although by this time you ought to be teachers, you need someone to reteach you the basic principles of God’s word. You need milk, not solid food!

5.web: For everyone who lives on milk is not experienced in the word of righteousness, for he is a baby.
5.kjv: For every one that useth milk is unskilful in the word of righteousness: for he is a babe.
5.bsb: For everyone who lives on milk is still an infant, inexperienced in the message of righteousness.

5.web: But solid food is for those who are full grown, who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern good and evil.
5.kjv: But strong meat belongeth to them that are of full age, even those who by reason of use have their senses exercised to discern both good and evil.
5.bsb: But solid food is for the mature, who by constant use have trained their senses to distinguish good from evil.

6.web: Therefore leaving the teaching of the first principles of Christ, let us press on to perfection—not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works, of faith toward God,
6.kjv: Therefore leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ, let us go on unto perfection; not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith toward God,
6.bsb: Therefore let us leave the elementary teachings about Christ and go on to maturity, not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works, and of faith in God,

6.web: of the teaching of baptisms, of laying on of hands, of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.
6.kjv: Of the doctrine of baptisms, and of laying on of hands, and of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.
6.bsb: instruction about baptisms, the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.

6.web: This will we do, if God permits.
6.kjv: And this will we do, if God permit.
6.bsb: And this we will do, if God permits.

6.web: For concerning those who were once enlightened and tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Spirit,
6.kjv: For it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost,
6.bsb: It is impossible for those who have once been enlightened, who have tasted the heavenly gift, who have shared in the Holy Spirit,

6.web: and tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the age to come,
6.kjv: And have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come,
6.bsb: who have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the powers of the coming age—

6.web: and then fell away, it is impossible to renew them again to repentance; seeing they crucify the Son of God for themselves again, and put him to open shame.
6.kjv: If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance; seeing they crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh, and put him to an open shame.
6.bsb: and then have fallen away—to be restored to repentance, because they themselves are crucifying the Son of God all over again and subjecting Him to open shame.

6.web: For the land which has drunk the rain that comes often on it, and produces a crop suitable for them for whose sake it is also tilled, receives blessing from God;
6.kjv: For the earth which drinketh in the rain that cometh oft upon it, and bringeth forth herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed, receiveth blessing from God:
6.bsb: For land that drinks in the rain often falling on it and that produces a crop useful to those for whom it is tended receives the blessing of God.

6.web: but if it bears thorns and thistles, it is rejected and near being cursed, whose end is to be burned.
6.kjv: But that which beareth thorns and briers is rejected, and is nigh unto cursing; whose end is to be burned.
6.bsb: But land that produces thorns and thistles is worthless, and its curse is imminent. In the end it will be burned.

6.web: But, beloved, we are persuaded of better things for you, and things that accompany salvation, even though we speak like this.
6.kjv: But, beloved, we are persuaded better things of you, and things that accompany salvation, though we thus speak.
6.bsb: Even though we speak like this, beloved, we are convinced of better things in your case—things that accompany salvation.

6.web: For God is not unrighteous, so as to forget your work and the labor of love which you showed toward his name, in that you served the saints, and still do serve them.
6.kjv: For God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labour of love, which ye have shewed toward his name, in that ye have ministered to the saints, and do minister.
6.bsb: For God is not unjust. He will not forget your work and the love you have shown for His name as you have ministered to the saints and continue to do so.

6.web: We desire that each one of you may show the same diligence to the fullness of hope even to the end,
6.kjv: And we desire that every one of you do shew the same diligence to the full assurance of hope unto the end:
6.bsb: We want each of you to show this same diligence to the very end, in order to make your hope sure.

6.web: that you won’t be sluggish, but imitators of those who through faith and perseverance inherited the promises.
6.kjv: That ye be not slothful, but followers of them who through faith and patience inherit the promises.
6.bsb: Then you will not be sluggish, but will imitate those who through faith and patience inherit what has been promised.

6.web: For when God made a promise to Abraham, since he could swear by no one greater, he swore by himself,
6.kjv: For when God made promise to Abraham, because he could swear by no greater, he sware by himself,
6.bsb: When God made His promise to Abraham, since He had no one greater to swear by, He swore by Himself,

6.web: saying, “Surely blessing I will bless you, and multiplying I will multiply you.”
6.kjv: Saying, Surely blessing I will bless thee, and multiplying I will multiply thee.
6.bsb: saying, “I will surely bless you and multiply your descendants.”

6.web: Thus, having patiently endured, he obtained the promise.
6.kjv: And so, after he had patiently endured, he obtained the promise.
6.bsb: And so Abraham, after waiting patiently, obtained the promise.

6.web: For men indeed swear by a greater one, and in every dispute of theirs the oath is final for confirmation.
6.kjv: For men verily swear by the greater: and an oath for confirmation is to them an end of all strife.
6.bsb: Men swear by someone greater than themselves, and their oath serves as a confirmation to end all argument.

6.web: In this way God, being determined to show more abundantly to the heirs of the promise the immutability of his counsel, interposed with an oath;
6.kjv: Wherein God, willing more abundantly to shew unto the heirs of promise the immutability of his counsel, confirmed it by an oath:
6.bsb: So when God wanted to make the unchanging nature of His purpose very clear to the heirs of the promise, He guaranteed it with an oath.

6.web: that by two immutable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we may have a strong encouragement, who have fled for refuge to take hold of the hope set before us.
6.kjv: That by two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation, who have fled for refuge to lay hold upon the hope set before us:
6.bsb: Thus by two unchangeable things in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have fled to take hold of the hope set before us may be strongly encouraged.

6.web: This hope we have as an anchor of the soul, a hope both sure and steadfast and entering into that which is within the veil;
6.kjv: Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and which entereth into that within the veil;
6.bsb: We have this hope as an anchor for the soul, firm and secure. It enters the inner sanctuary behind the curtain,

6.web: where as a forerunner Jesus entered for us, having become a high priest forever after the order of Melchizedek.
6.kjv: Whither the forerunner is for us entered, even Jesus, made an high priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
6.bsb: where Jesus our forerunner has entered on our behalf. He has become a high priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.

7.web: For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,
7.kjv: For this Melchisedec, king of Salem, priest of the most high God, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him;
7.bsb: This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,

7.web: to whom also Abraham divided a tenth part of all (being first, by interpretation, “king of righteousness”, and then also “king of Salem”, which means “king of peace”;
7.kjv: To whom also Abraham gave a tenth part of all; first being by interpretation King of righteousness, and after that also King of Salem, which is, King of peace;
7.bsb: and Abraham apportioned to him a tenth of everything. First, his name means “king of righteousness.” Then also, “king of Salem” means “king of peace.”

7.web: without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but made like the Son of God), remains a priest continually.
7.kjv: Without father, without mother, without descent, having neither beginning of days, nor end of life; but made like unto the Son of God; abideth a priest continually.
7.bsb: Without father or mother or genealogy, without beginning of days or end of life, like the Son of God, he remains a priest for all time.

7.web: Now consider how great this man was, to whom even Abraham, the patriarch, gave a tenth out of the best plunder.
7.kjv: Now consider how great this man was , unto whom even the patriarch Abraham gave the tenth of the spoils.
7.bsb: Consider how great Melchizedek was: Even the patriarch Abraham gave him a tenth of the plunder.

7.web: They indeed of the sons of Levi who receive the priest’s office have a commandment to take tithes of the people according to the law, that is, of their brothers, though these have come out of the body of Abraham,
7.kjv: And verily they that are of the sons of Levi, who receive the office of the priesthood, have a commandment to take tithes of the people according to the law, that is, of their brethren, though they come out of the loins of Abraham:
7.bsb: Now the law commands the sons of Levi who become priests to collect a tenth from the people—that is, from their brothers—though they too are descended from Abraham.

7.web: but he whose genealogy is not counted from them has accepted tithes from Abraham, and has blessed him who has the promises.
7.kjv: But he whose descent is not counted from them received tithes of Abraham, and blessed him that had the promises.
7.bsb: But Melchizedek, who did not trace his descent from Levi, collected a tenth from Abraham and blessed him who had the promises.

7.web: But without any dispute the lesser is blessed by the greater.
7.kjv: And without all contradiction the less is blessed of the better.
7.bsb: And indisputably, the lesser is blessed by the greater.

7.web: Here people who die receive tithes, but there one receives tithes of whom it is testified that he lives.
7.kjv: And here men that die receive tithes; but there he receiveth them , of whom it is witnessed that he liveth.
7.bsb: In the case of the Levites, mortal men collect the tenth; but in the case of Melchizedek, it is affirmed that he lives on.

7.web: We can say that through Abraham even Levi, who receives tithes, has paid tithes,
7.kjv: And as I may so say, Levi also, who receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham.
7.bsb: And so to speak, Levi, who collects the tenth, paid the tenth through Abraham.

7.web: for he was yet in the body of his father when Melchizedek met him.
7.kjv: For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him.
7.bsb: For when Melchizedek met Abraham, Levi was still in the loin of his ancestor.

7.web: Now if there were perfection through the Levitical priesthood (for under it the people have received the law), what further need was there for another priest to arise after the order of Melchizedek, and not be called after the order of Aaron?
7.kjv: If therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, (for under it the people received the law,) what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron?
7.bsb: Now if perfection could have been attained through the Levitical priesthood (for on this basis the people received the law), why was there still need for another priest to appear—one in the order of Melchizedek and not in the order of Aaron?

7.web: For the priesthood being changed, there is of necessity a change made also in the law.
7.kjv: For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law.
7.bsb: For when the priesthood is changed, the law must be changed as well.

7.web: For he of whom these things are said belongs to another tribe, from which no one has officiated at the altar.
7.kjv: For he of whom these things are spoken pertaineth to another tribe, of which no man gave attendance at the altar.
7.bsb: He of whom these things are said belonged to a different tribe, from which no one has ever served at the altar.

7.web: For it is evident that our Lord has sprung out of Judah, about which tribe Moses spoke nothing concerning priesthood.
7.kjv: For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.
7.bsb: For it is clear that our Lord descended from Judah, a tribe as to which Moses said nothing about priests.

7.web: This is yet more abundantly evident, if after the likeness of Melchizedek there arises another priest,
7.kjv: And it is yet far more evident: for that after the similitude of Melchisedec there ariseth another priest,
7.bsb: And this point is even more clear if another priest like Melchizedek appears,

7.web: who has been made, not after the law of a fleshly commandment, but after the power of an endless life:
7.kjv: Who is made, not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life.
7.bsb: one who has become a priest not by a law of succession, but by the power of an indestructible life.

7.web: for it is testified, “You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.”
7.kjv: For he testifieth, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.
7.bsb: For it is testified: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”

7.web: For there is an annulling of a foregoing commandment because of its weakness and uselessness
7.kjv: For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof.
7.bsb: So the former commandment is set aside because it was weak and useless

7.web: (for the law made nothing perfect), and a bringing in of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
7.kjv: For the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope did ; by the which we draw nigh unto God.
7.bsb: (for the law made nothing perfect), and a better hope is introduced, by which we draw near to God.

7.web: Inasmuch as he was not made priest without the taking of an oath
7.kjv: And inasmuch as not without an oath he was made priest :
7.bsb: And none of this happened without an oath. For others became priests without an oath,

7.web: (for they indeed have been made priests without an oath), but he with an oath by him that says of him, “The Lord swore and will not change his mind, ‘You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.’”
7.kjv: (For those priests were made without an oath; but this with an oath by him that said unto him, The Lord sware and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec:)
7.bsb: but Jesus became a priest with an oath by the One who said to Him: “The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind: ‘You are a priest forever.’”

7.web: By so much, Jesus has become the collateral of a better covenant.
7.kjv: By so much was Jesus made a surety of a better testament.
7.bsb: Because of this oath, Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant.

7.web: Many, indeed, have been made priests, because they are hindered from continuing by death.
7.kjv: And they truly were many priests, because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death:
7.bsb: Now there have been many other priests, since death prevented them from continuing in office.

7.web: But he, because he lives forever, has his priesthood unchangeable.
7.kjv: But this man , because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood.
7.bsb: But because Jesus lives forever, He has a permanent priesthood.

7.web: Therefore he is also able to save to the uttermost those who draw near to God through him, seeing that he lives forever to make intercession for them.
7.kjv: Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.
7.bsb: Therefore He is able to save completely those who draw near to God through Him, since He always lives to intercede for them.

7.web: For such a high priest was fitting for us: holy, guiltless, undefiled, separated from sinners, and made higher than the heavens;
7.kjv: For such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens;
7.bsb: Such a high priest truly befits us—One who is holy, innocent, undefiled, set apart from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.

7.web: who doesn’t need, like those high priests, to offer up sacrifices daily, first for his own sins, and then for the sins of the people. For he did this once for all, when he offered up himself.
7.kjv: Who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people’s: for this he did once, when he offered up himself.
7.bsb: Unlike the other high priests, He does not need to offer daily sacrifices, first for His own sins and then for the sins of the people; He sacrificed for sin once for all when He offered up Himself.

7.web: For the law appoints men as high priests who have weakness, but the word of the oath which came after the law appoints a Son forever who has been perfected.
7.kjv: For the law maketh men high priests which have infirmity; but the word of the oath, which was since the law, maketh the Son, who is consecrated for evermore.
7.bsb: For the law appoints as high priests men who are weak; but the oath, which came after the law, appointed the Son, who has been made perfect forever.

8.web: Now in the things which we are saying, the main point is this. We have such a high priest, who sat down on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens,
8.kjv: Now of the things which we have spoken this is the sum: We have such an high priest, who is set on the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in the heavens;
8.bsb: The point of what we are saying is this: We do have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven,

8.web: a servant of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, not man.
8.kjv: A minister of the sanctuary, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man.
8.bsb: and who ministers in the sanctuary and true tabernacle set up by the Lord, not by man.

8.web: For every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices. Therefore it is necessary that this high priest also have something to offer.
8.kjv: For every high priest is ordained to offer gifts and sacrifices: wherefore it is of necessity that this man have somewhat also to offer.
8.bsb: And since every high priest is appointed to offer both gifts and sacrifices, it was necessary for this One also to have something to offer.

8.web: For if he were on earth, he would not be a priest at all, seeing there are priests who offer the gifts according to the law;
8.kjv: For if he were on earth, he should not be a priest, seeing that there are priests that offer gifts according to the law:
8.bsb: Now if He were on earth, He would not be a priest, since there are already priests who offer gifts according to the law.

8.web: who serve a copy and shadow of the heavenly things, even as Moses was warned by God when he was about to make the tabernacle, for he said, “See, you shall make everything according to the pattern that was shown to you on the mountain.”
8.kjv: Who serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.
8.bsb: The place where they serve is a copy and shadow of what is in heaven. This is why Moses was warned when he was about to build the tabernacle: “See to it that you make everything according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.”

8.web: But now he has obtained a more excellent ministry, by so much as he is also the mediator of a better covenant, which on better promises has been given as law.
8.kjv: But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises.
8.bsb: Now, however, Jesus has received a much more excellent ministry, just as the covenant He mediates is better and is founded on better promises.

8.web: For if that first covenant had been faultless, then no place would have been sought for a second.
8.kjv: For if that first covenant had been faultless, then should no place have been sought for the second.
8.bsb: For if that first covenant had been without fault, no place would have been sought for a second.

8.web: For finding fault with them, he said, “Behold, the days come”, says the Lord, “that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah;
8.kjv: For finding fault with them, he saith, Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah:
8.bsb: But God found fault with the people and said: “Behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.

8.web: not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers, in the day that I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; for they didn’t continue in my covenant, and I disregarded them,” says the Lord.
8.kjv: Not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers in the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt; because they continued not in my covenant, and I regarded them not, saith the Lord.
8.bsb: It will not be like the covenant I made with their fathers when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not abide by My covenant, and I disregarded them, declares the Lord.

8.web: “For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel. After those days,” says the Lord; “I will put my laws into their mind, I will also write them on their heart. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
8.kjv: For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith the Lord; I will put my laws into their mind, and write them in their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people:
8.bsb: For this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the Lord. I will put My laws in their minds and inscribe them on their hearts. And I will be their God, and they will be My people.

8.web: They will not teach every man his fellow citizen, and every man his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ for all will know me, from their least to their greatest.
8.kjv: And they shall not teach every man his neighbour, and every man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest.
8.bsb: No longer will each one teach his neighbor or his brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ because they will all know Me, from the least of them to the greatest.

8.web: For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness. I will remember their sins and lawless deeds no more.”
8.kjv: For I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins and their iniquities will I remember no more.
8.bsb: For I will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins no more.”

8.web: In that he says, “A new covenant”, he has made the first old. But that which is becoming old and grows aged is near to vanishing away.
8.kjv: In that he saith, A new covenant , he hath made the first old. Now that which decayeth and waxeth old is ready to vanish away.
8.bsb: By speaking of a new covenant, He has made the first one obsolete; and what is obsolete and aging will soon disappear.

9.web: Now indeed even the first covenant had ordinances of divine service, and an earthly sanctuary.
9.kjv: Then verily the first covenant had also ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary.
9.bsb: Now the first covenant had regulations for worship and also an earthly sanctuary.

9.web: For a tabernacle was prepared. In the first part were the lamp stand, the table, and the show bread; which is called the Holy Place.
9.kjv: For there was a tabernacle made; the first, wherein was the candlestick, and the table, and the shewbread; which is called the sanctuary.
9.bsb: A tabernacle was prepared. In its first room were the lampstand, the table, and the consecrated bread. This was called the Holy Place.

9.web: After the second veil was the tabernacle which is called the Holy of Holies,
9.kjv: And after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all;
9.bsb: Behind the second curtain was a room called the Most Holy Place,

9.web: having a golden altar of incense, and the ark of the covenant overlaid on all sides with gold, in which was a golden pot holding the manna, Aaron’s rod that budded, and the tablets of the covenant;
9.kjv: Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron’s rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant;
9.bsb: containing the golden altar of incense and the gold-covered ark of the covenant. Inside the ark were the gold jar of manna, Aaron’s staff that had budded, and the stone tablets of the covenant.

9.web: and above it cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat, of which things we can’t speak now in detail.
9.kjv: And over it the cherubims of glory shadowing the mercyseat; of which we cannot now speak particularly.
9.bsb: Above the ark were the cherubim of glory, overshadowing the mercy seat. But we cannot discuss these things in detail now.

9.web: Now these things having been thus prepared, the priests go in continually into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the services,
9.kjv: Now when these things were thus ordained, the priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God .
9.bsb: When everything had been prepared in this way, the priests entered regularly into the first room to perform their sacred duties.

9.web: but into the second the high priest alone, once in the year, not without blood, which he offers for himself, and for the errors of the people.
9.kjv: But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people:
9.bsb: But only the high priest entered the second room, and then only once a year, and never without blood, which he offered for himself and for the sins the people had committed in ignorance.

9.web: The Holy Spirit is indicating this, that the way into the Holy Place wasn’t yet revealed while the first tabernacle was still standing;
9.kjv: The Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing:
9.bsb: By this arrangement the Holy Spirit was showing that the way into the Most Holy Place had not yet been disclosed as long as the first tabernacle was still standing.

9.web: which is a symbol of the present age, where gifts and sacrifices are offered that are incapable, concerning the conscience, of making the worshiper perfect;
9.kjv: Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience;
9.bsb: It is an illustration for the present time, because the gifts and sacrifices being offered were unable to cleanse the conscience of the worshiper.

9.web: being only (with meats and drinks and various washings) fleshly ordinances, imposed until a time of reformation.
9.kjv: Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.
9.bsb: They consist only in food and drink and special washings—external regulations imposed until the time of reform.

9.web: But Christ having come as a high priest of the coming good things, through the greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this creation,
9.kjv: But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands, that is to say, not of this building;
9.bsb: But when Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come, He went through the greater and more perfect tabernacle that is not made by hands and is not a part of this creation.

9.web: nor yet through the blood of goats and calves, but through his own blood, entered in once for all into the Holy Place, having obtained eternal redemption.
9.kjv: Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us .
9.bsb: He did not enter by the blood of goats and calves, but He entered the Most Holy Place once for all by His own blood, thus securing eternal redemption.

9.web: For if the blood of goats and bulls, and the ashes of a heifer sprinkling those who have been defiled, sanctify to the cleanness of the flesh:
9.kjv: For if the blood of bulls and of goats, and the ashes of an heifer sprinkling the unclean, sanctifieth to the purifying of the flesh:
9.bsb: For if the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those who are ceremonially unclean sanctify them so that their bodies are clean,

9.web: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without defect to God, cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?
9.kjv: How much more shall the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to God, purge your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?
9.bsb: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered Himself unblemished to God, purify our consciences from works of death, so that we may serve the living God!

9.web: For this reason he is the mediator of a new covenant, since a death has occurred for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first covenant, that those who have been called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.
9.kjv: And for this cause he is the mediator of the new testament, that by means of death, for the redemption of the transgressions that were under the first testament, they which are called might receive the promise of eternal inheritance.
9.bsb: Therefore Christ is the mediator of a new covenant, so that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance, now that He has died to redeem them from the transgressions committed under the first covenant.

9.web: For where a last will and testament is, there must of necessity be the death of him who made it.
9.kjv: For where a testament is , there must also of necessity be the death of the testator.
9.bsb: In the case of a will, it is necessary to establish the death of the one who made it,

9.web: For a will is in force where there has been death, for it is never in force while he who made it lives.
9.kjv: For a testament is of force after men are dead: otherwise it is of no strength at all while the testator liveth.
9.bsb: because a will does not take effect until the one who made it has died; it cannot be executed while he is still alive.

9.web: Therefore even the first covenant has not been dedicated without blood.
9.kjv: Whereupon neither the first testament was dedicated without blood.
9.bsb: That is why even the first covenant was not put into effect without blood.

9.web: For when every commandment had been spoken by Moses to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of the calves and the goats, with water and scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book itself and all the people,
9.kjv: For when Moses had spoken every precept to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and of goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book, and all the people,
9.bsb: For when Moses had proclaimed every commandment of the law to all the people, he took the blood of calves and goats, along with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled the scroll and all the people,

9.web: saying, “This is the blood of the covenant which God has commanded you.”
9.kjv: Saying, This is the blood of the testament which God hath enjoined unto you.
9.bsb: saying, “This is the blood of the covenant, which God has commanded you to keep.”

9.web: Moreover he sprinkled the tabernacle and all the vessels of the ministry in the same way with the blood.
9.kjv: Moreover he sprinkled with blood both the tabernacle, and all the vessels of the ministry.
9.bsb: In the same way, he sprinkled with blood the tabernacle and all the vessels used in worship.

9.web: According to the law, nearly everything is cleansed with blood, and apart from shedding of blood there is no remission.
9.kjv: And almost all things are by the law purged with blood; and without shedding of blood is no remission.
9.bsb: According to the law, in fact, nearly everything must be purified with blood, and without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.

9.web: It was necessary therefore that the copies of the things in the heavens should be cleansed with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
9.kjv: It was therefore necessary that the patterns of things in the heavens should be purified with these; but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
9.bsb: So it was necessary for the copies of the heavenly things to be purified with these sacrifices, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.

9.web: For Christ hasn’t entered into holy places made with hands, which are representations of the true, but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us;
9.kjv: For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands, which are the figures of the true; but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us:
9.bsb: For Christ did not enter a man-made copy of the true sanctuary, but He entered heaven itself, now to appear on our behalf in the presence of God.

9.web: nor yet that he should offer himself often, as the high priest enters into the holy place year by year with blood not his own,
9.kjv: Nor yet that he should offer himself often, as the high priest entereth into the holy place every year with blood of others;
9.bsb: Nor did He enter heaven to offer Himself again and again, as the high priest enters the Most Holy Place every year with blood that is not his own.

9.web: or else he must have suffered often since the foundation of the world. But now once at the end of the ages, he has been revealed to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.
9.kjv: For then must he often have suffered since the foundation of the world: but now once in the end of the world hath he appeared to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.
9.bsb: Otherwise, Christ would have had to suffer repeatedly since the foundation of the world. But now He has appeared once for all at the end of the ages to do away with sin by the sacrifice of Himself.

9.web: Inasmuch as it is appointed for men to die once, and after this, judgment,
9.kjv: And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment:
9.bsb: Just as man is appointed to die once, and after that to face judgment,

9.web: so Christ also, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, without sin, to those who are eagerly waiting for him for salvation.
9.kjv: So Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many; and unto them that look for him shall he appear the second time without sin unto salvation.
9.bsb: so also Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many; and He will appear a second time, not to bear sin, but to bring salvation to those who eagerly await Him.

10.web: For the law, having a shadow of the good to come, not the very image of the things, can never with the same sacrifices year by year, which they offer continually, make perfect those who draw near.
10.kjv: For the law having a shadow of good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with those sacrifices which they offered year by year continually make the comers thereunto perfect.
10.bsb: For the law is only a shadow of the good things to come, not the realities themselves. It can never, by the same sacrifices offered year after year, make perfect those who draw near to worship.

10.web: Or else wouldn’t they have ceased to be offered, because the worshipers, having been once cleansed, would have had no more consciousness of sins?
10.kjv: For then would they not have ceased to be offered? because that the worshippers once purged should have had no more conscience of sins.
10.bsb: If it could, would not the offerings have ceased? For the worshipers would have been cleansed once for all, and would no longer have felt the guilt of their sins.

10.web: But in those sacrifices there is a yearly reminder of sins.
10.kjv: But in those sacrifices there is a remembrance again made of sins every year.
10.bsb: Instead, those sacrifices are an annual reminder of sins,

10.web: For it is impossible that the blood of bulls and goats should take away sins.
10.kjv: For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.
10.bsb: because it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.

10.web: Therefore when he comes into the world, he says, “Sacrifice and offering you didn’t desire, but you prepared a body for me.
10.kjv: Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me:
10.bsb: Therefore, when Christ came into the world, He said: “Sacrifice and offering You did not desire, but a body You prepared for Me.

10.web: You had no pleasure in whole burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin.
10.kjv: In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure.
10.bsb: In burnt offerings and sin offerings You took no delight.

10.web: Then I said, ‘Behold, I have come (in the scroll of the book it is written of me) to do your will, O God.’”
10.kjv: Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.
10.bsb: Then I said, ‘Here I am, it is written about Me in the scroll: I have come to do Your will, O God.’”

10.web: Previously saying, “Sacrifices and offerings and whole burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin you didn’t desire, neither had pleasure in them” (those which are offered according to the law),
10.kjv: Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein ; which are offered by the law;
10.bsb: In the passage above He says, “Sacrifices and offerings, burnt offerings and sin offerings You did not desire, nor did You delight in them” (although they are offered according to the law).

10.web: then he has said, “Behold, I have come to do your will.” He takes away the first, that he may establish the second,
10.kjv: Then said he, Lo, I come to do thy will, O God. He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.
10.bsb: Then He adds, “Here I am, I have come to do Your will.” He takes away the first to establish the second.

10.web: by which will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
10.kjv: By the which will we are sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all .
10.bsb: And by that will, we have been sanctified through the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.

10.web: Every priest indeed stands day by day serving and often offering the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins,
10.kjv: And every priest standeth daily ministering and offering oftentimes the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins:
10.bsb: Day after day every priest stands to minister and to offer again and again the same sacrifices, which can never take away sins.

10.web: but he, when he had offered one sacrifice for sins forever, sat down on the right hand of God;
10.kjv: But this man, after he had offered one sacrifice for sins for ever, sat down on the right hand of God;
10.bsb: But when this Priest had offered for all time one sacrifice for sins, He sat down at the right hand of God.

10.web: from that time waiting until his enemies are made the footstool of his feet.
10.kjv: From henceforth expecting till his enemies be made his footstool.
10.bsb: Since that time, He waits for His enemies to be made a footstool for His feet,

10.web: For by one offering he has perfected forever those who are being sanctified.
10.kjv: For by one offering he hath perfected for ever them that are sanctified.
10.bsb: because by a single offering He has made perfect for all time those who are being sanctified.

10.web: The Holy Spirit also testifies to us, for after saying,
10.kjv: Whereof the Holy Ghost also is a witness to us: for after that he had said before,
10.bsb: The Holy Spirit also testifies to us about this. First He says:

10.web: “This is the covenant that I will make with them: ‘After those days,’ says the Lord, ‘I will put my laws on their heart, I will also write them on their mind;’” then he says,
10.kjv: This is the covenant that I will make with them after those days, saith the Lord, I will put my laws into their hearts, and in their minds will I write them;
10.bsb: “This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, declares the Lord. I will put My laws in their hearts and inscribe them on their minds.”

10.web: “I will remember their sins and their iniquities no more.”
10.kjv: And their sins and iniquities will I remember no more.
10.bsb: Then He adds: “Their sins and lawless acts I will remember no more.”

10.web: Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin.
10.kjv: Now where remission of these is, there is no more offering for sin.
10.bsb: And where these have been forgiven, an offering for sin is no longer needed.

10.web: Having therefore, brothers, boldness to enter into the holy place by the blood of Jesus,
10.kjv: Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus,
10.bsb: Therefore, brothers, since we have confidence to enter the Most Holy Place by the blood of Jesus,

10.web: by the way which he dedicated for us, a new and living way, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh;
10.kjv: By a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh;
10.bsb: by the new and living way opened for us through the curtain of His body,

10.web: and having a great priest over God’s house,
10.kjv: And having an high priest over the house of God;
10.bsb: and since we have a great priest over the house of God,

10.web: let’s draw near with a true heart in fullness of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and having our body washed with pure water,
10.kjv: Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience, and our bodies washed with pure water.
10.bsb: let us draw near with a sincere heart in full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled to cleanse us from a guilty conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.

10.web: let us hold fast the confession of our hope without wavering; for he who promised is faithful.
10.kjv: Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised;)
10.bsb: Let us hold resolutely to the hope we profess, for He who promised is faithful.

10.web: Let us consider how to provoke one another to love and good works,
10.kjv: And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works:
10.bsb: And let us consider how to spur one another on to love and good deeds.

10.web: not forsaking our own assembling together, as the custom of some is, but exhorting one another; and so much the more, as you see the Day approaching.
10.kjv: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is ; but exhorting one another : and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.
10.bsb: Let us not neglect meeting together, as some have made a habit, but let us encourage one another, and all the more as you see the Day approaching.

10.web: For if we sin willfully after we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remains no more a sacrifice for sins,
10.kjv: For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins,
10.bsb: If we deliberately go on sinning after we have received the knowledge of the truth, no further sacrifice for sins remains,

10.web: but a certain fearful expectation of judgment, and a fierceness of fire which will devour the adversaries.
10.kjv: But a certain fearful looking for of judgment and fiery indignation, which shall devour the adversaries.
10.bsb: but only a fearful expectation of judgment and of raging fire that will consume all adversaries.

10.web: A man who disregards Moses’ law dies without compassion on the word of two or three witnesses.
10.kjv: He that despised Moses’ law died without mercy under two or three witnesses:
10.bsb: Anyone who rejected the law of Moses died without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

10.web: How much worse punishment do you think he will be judged worthy of who has trodden under foot the Son of God, and has counted the blood of the covenant with which he was sanctified an unholy thing, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?
10.kjv: Of how much sorer punishment, suppose ye, shall he be thought worthy, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God, and hath counted the blood of the covenant, wherewith he was sanctified, an unholy thing, and hath done despite unto the Spirit of grace?
10.bsb: How much more severely do you think one deserves to be punished who has trampled on the Son of God, profaned the blood of the covenant that sanctified him, and insulted the Spirit of grace?

10.web: For we know him who said, “Vengeance belongs to me,” says the Lord, “I will repay.” Again, “The Lord will judge his people.”
10.kjv: For we know him that hath said, Vengeance belongeth unto me, I will recompense, saith the Lord. And again, The Lord shall judge his people.
10.bsb: For we know Him who said, “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay,” and again, “The Lord will judge His people.”

10.web: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
10.kjv: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
10.bsb: It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

10.web: But remember the former days, in which, after you were enlightened, you endured a great struggle with sufferings;
10.kjv: But call to remembrance the former days, in which, after ye were illuminated, ye endured a great fight of afflictions;
10.bsb: Remember the early days that you were in the light. In those days, you endured a great conflict in the face of suffering.

10.web: partly, being exposed to both reproaches and oppressions; and partly, becoming partakers with those who were treated so.
10.kjv: Partly, whilst ye were made a gazingstock both by reproaches and afflictions; and partly, whilst ye became companions of them that were so used.
10.bsb: Sometimes you were publicly exposed to ridicule and persecution; at other times you were partners with those who were so treated.

10.web: For you both had compassion on me in my chains, and joyfully accepted the plundering of your possessions, knowing that you have for yourselves a better possession and an enduring one in the heavens.
10.kjv: For ye had compassion of me in my bonds, and took joyfully the spoiling of your goods, knowing in yourselves that ye have in heaven a better and an enduring substance.
10.bsb: You sympathized with those in prison and joyfully accepted the confiscation of your property, knowing that you yourselves had a better and permanent possession.

10.web: Therefore don’t throw away your boldness, which has a great reward.
10.kjv: Cast not away therefore your confidence, which hath great recompence of reward.
10.bsb: So do not throw away your confidence; it holds a great reward.
